newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Provisions, charges push UBS to 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Provisions, charges push UBS to 1996 loss.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) reported on Friday a 1996 group net loss of 348 million francs ($235.7 million) after big special provisions for credit risks and restructuring charges but said operating results were good.
It had posted a 1.68 billion franc group profit in 1995.
The loss was expected after UBS said last November it would take one-time charges of three billion francs to cover bad domestic loans and of 120 million for Swiss restructuring.
"UBS reported a good operating result for 1996. Cash flow was increased by 21 percent to 4,312 million Swiss francs," it said in a statement before a news conference.

"The special provision of three billion francs, announced in November 1996, for credit risks over the next few years and a charge of a 120 million francs for restructuring costs in Switzerland resulted in the UBS group reporting a loss of 348 million francs for 1996, however."
Ordinary credit risk provisions of 1.4 billion also weighed on results, it said.
Excluding the special provision and restructuring charge, "group profit would have been in the region of 1.8 billion francs, seven percent more than in 1995", it said. ($ = 1.476 Swiss Francs)
